headline: Broad networked CRM agent paired with Semantic Kernel can leak data and cascade errors through shared MCP/filesystem paths; prompt-injection risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or an MCP server, and Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and plugins. That shared instruction channel makes prompt injection plausible if aci ingests untrusted content and SK forwards it into tool calls. No explicit provenance tracking is shown, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF aci forwards untrusted text into MCP/tool prompts
IF Semantic Kernel routes plugin outputs back into agent instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every MCP message
Block raw HTML/markdown from entering tool prompts
Require a human review step before executing tool-derived instructions
Restrict MCP servers to allowlisted schemas
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress. Semantic Kernel can read/write application-defined files and call external model providers and MCP servers. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive data can flow from aci into SK and then out to third-party APIs by default.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, memory store, or MCP-backed context
IF SK sends application context to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face or another external API
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Disable file ingestion for sensitive folders
Route sensitive prompts through a local-only model
Turn off shared memory-store sync for CRM/email data
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before outbound API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API access, while Semantic Kernel supports multiple instances, write_filesystem, and shared state via memory store. Even without shell or git writes, overlapping mutable resources and concurrent instances can overwrite each other's files or context in default orchestration setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application-defined files or shared memory entries
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or per-agent namespaces
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Namespace shared memory keys by agent ID
Enable optimistic-lock checks on writes
Serialize writes to shared resources
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Semantic Kernel is a library that can execute plugin/tool workflows. If SK treats aci output as authoritative, a mistaken lead, email, or calendar action can be propagated into downstream side effects without verification, creating irreversible operational errors.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes aci output as trusted input
IF downstream plugins send email, update CRM records, or schedule calendar events without validation
mitigations: Require schema validation on aci outputs
Add a confirmation step before external actions
Log and diff proposed vs. executed changes
Limit SK to read-only mode for aci-derived data
requires-engineering: implement action approval gates

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, calendar, and customer support data, while Semantic Kernel can move application context through external model providers and plugins. The pair therefore creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch if regulated customer data is routed into SK-backed APIs or memory stores, though no specific jurisdiction is documented.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is placed into SK prompts, plugins, or memory stores
IF the chosen model provider or plugin has stricter retention or residency terms than aci's source systems
mitigations: Classify regulated fields before routing them to SK
Block PHI/PII from external model calls
Document retention settings for each plugin/provider
Use region-pinned deployments where available
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency
